name: Influenza (flu)
summary: Seasonal vaccines that protect against influenza, generally recommended for people aged six months and older.
descriptionParagraphs: Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. CDC recommends seasonal flu vaccination for most people aged six months and older, with some products limited to particular age groups or health histories.

Flu vaccines come as inactivated, recombinant or live attenuated products. Most are given by injection; an eligible nasal-spray formulation is also available. Children may need two doses in their first vaccination season. Confirm the right product and timing with a qualified provider.
ageGroup: Generally people aged 6 months and older, with product-specific restrictions
vaccineType: Inactivated, recombinant or live attenuated, depending on product
administrationMethod: Injection, or an eligible nasal-spray formulation
scheduleSummary: Seasonal vaccination; number of doses depends on age and vaccination history

name: COVID-19
summary: Vaccines that protect against COVID-19; eligibility and timing depend on age, product, risk and current CDC guidance.
descriptionParagraphs: COVID-19 is a respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Recommendations for who should receive a COVID-19 vaccine, and when, depend on age, the specific product, individual risk and current clinical guidance, which CDC updates for each season.

Available products use different approaches, including mRNA and protein-based vaccines, and all are given by injection. Because the schedule changes over time, VaxAccess does not publish a fixed seasonal schedule; follow CDC's current guidance and confirm with a qualified provider.

externalLinks.label: CDC: Staying up to date with COVID-19 vaccines

ageGroup: Depends on age, product, risk and current guidance
vaccineType: Product-dependent, including mRNA and protein-based vaccines
scheduleSummary: Timing and number of doses depend on current guidance and individual history

name: Mpox
summary: Vaccination for people who meet mpox exposure or risk criteria; the documented Austin clinic used the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine.
descriptionParagraphs: Mpox is a viral disease that spreads mainly through close, often skin-to-skin, contact. CDC recommends vaccination for people who meet exposure or risk criteria; administration by age requires review by a provider.

The Austin clinic documented on this site used JYNNEOS, a live, nonreplicating vaccine. It is given by subcutaneous injection or, where eligible, intradermal injection. The cited CDC guidance describes two doses given four weeks apart. Confirm eligibility and timing with a qualified provider.
ageGroup: People meeting exposure or risk criteria; age-specific use requires provider review
vaccineType: Live, nonreplicating (JYNNEOS, used at the documented event)
scheduleSummary: Two doses four weeks apart, per cited CDC guidance
